observables.rationale: MAPPING: The phospho-specific antibody reports the phosphorylated species only, so the observable is Rp alone and not a sum over R and Rp. Linear transformation: the noise is additive in densitometry units and the data include values at and below zero, which a log transformation cannot represent. NOISE + TRANSFORMATION: Additive normal noise with a single constant sigma across doses and times. The replicate spread does not grow with signal level — the two lanes differ by a similar absolute amount at the plateau as at t=0 — which rules out a proportional or log-normal error model. Sigma is estimated because no error column was supplied; two replicates per point is too few to fix it empirically per condition. SCALING: The readout is uncalibrated densitometry in arbitrary units, so the simulated Rp and the measured column are not in the same units and a scale factor is mandatory — without it the magnitude-reconciliation gate has no way to pass. No offset: the description says the values are already background-subtracted and that t=0 lanes sit at or near zero, so a free additive term would be fitting the background twice. Shared across conditions because all three doses were blotted on the same lysate series with one antibody and one exposure; a per-dose scale would absorb the dose response itself and destroy the prediction being asked for.
